newsitem.title: UK: Tate and Lyle up on positive outlook.
newsitem.headline: Tate and Lyle up on positive outlook.

text.p: Shares in Tate and Lyle rose to a five week high after the UK starch and sugar producer said its underperforming North American unit should benefit from better market conditions this year, dealers said.
By 1120 GMT, the shares were up 11-1/2p to 481-1/2p.
Tate and Lyle forecasted better results from Staley, the company's beleagured North American wet corn miller
"The statement was quite positive," said one marketmaker. "It looks like it's hit the bottom of the cycle.
Tate and Lyle also reported full-year pretax profits of 276.3 million stg, which was on the low end of analysts' forecasts, and issued a dividend of 17p per share, as expected.
Technical analyst Richard Marshall said he was targeting the 500p level for the stock. A rally above that level would portend a move to 550p, he said.
However, chart indicators suggest that the share price is likely to remain between 450p and 500p, where they've been trapped for the past twelve months, Marshall added.
